title: Frontend Performance: Core Web Vitals, Rendering & Data Loading
concept: Make a React / Next.js app fast where users feel it: Core Web Vitals from real users (web-vitals), long tasks and scheduler.yield, debounce and throttle, list virtualization, memoization in the React Compiler era, request waterfalls, HTTP caching with stale-while-revalidate, and Lighthouse CI budgets. Challenges are JavaScript modules graded against a simulated browser main thread and network.
description: Make a React / Next.js app fast where users feel it: Core Web Vitals from real users (web-vitals), long tasks and scheduler.yield, debounce and throttle, list virtualization, memoization in the React Compiler era, request waterfalls, HTTP caching with stale-while-revalidate, and Lighthouse CI budgets. 8 lessons on one project, each applying the tool to a real production situation, with 1-2 graded challenges per lesson.

learningOutcomes.text: Measure LCP, INP and CLS from real users and find the element or interaction behind a bad score.
Keep the main thread free for input: yield in long tasks, debounce and throttle event handlers.
Render only what changes: virtualized lists and memoization that pays for itself.
Remove request waterfalls, cache with the right HTTP headers and stop regressions with budgets in CI.

knownIssues: Challenges grade JavaScript against a simulated main thread, network and render counter, not a real browser.
